michelle-barratt.p: Michelle Barratt is a Clinical Psychologist who specialises in:
Qualifications: BA. Psych. Sc., BA. Psych. Sc. (Hons)., Masters of Clinical Psychology. Honorary Member of APS, AHPRA Endorsed-Clinical Psychology.

About Michelle: Michelle is a Brisbane Clinical Psychologist who was born in Zimbabwe and immigrated to Australia in 2001. She has two adult children and has gained a wealth of experience managing complex family situations amid conflict.

Her psychological practice’s main aim and her mandate to clinicians who work with her in Michelle Barratt Psychology is to build upon the strengths within each person and to support them to engage effectively in therapy to develop a sound sense of self that is central to formulating their own identity. We face problems every day of our lives, but if we have high self-esteem, we can invariably work through the problems that face us; by building an awareness of who we are in this world, we become empowered to find hope and make our dreams and ideas become a reality. However, we also need to be mindful of others, so that we can develop a balance that secures us in this world while fostering relationships with others, including within our families, friendships, and the workplace.
Michelle’s private practice primarily works with the above values in mind and embraces working with adults, children, adolescents, couples and families.

Michelle has previously worked at the Prince Charles Hospital, Chermside, Brisbane, Queensland in the Adult Mental Health Outpatient Centre in 2011, which included developing complex treatment plans for clients that required a range of support; these included:

list: Anxiety Disorders (Acute Stress Disorder, Social Anxiety, Generalised Anxiety Disorder (GAD)
Abuse: Psychological, Verbal, Domestic Violence, Child Abuse/Neglect, and Financial

michelle-barratt.p: While this role focused on supporting the client’s overall mental health, it also ensured and involved “wrap-around care” for the client, which meant that Michelle worked within a multi-disciplinary team that included: psychiatrists, occupational therapists, nurses, social workers, other psychologists, and recruitment offices. This was to ensure that the best and most appropriate support and care for each and every client was sought, so that they felt supported, understood and validated in their particular individual needs.

Michelle worked with Kids Helpline for 2 years. She offered her professional skills in working with children, adolescents, and young adults in crisis. The ages ranged from children as young as 5 to young adults of 25.

Michelle’s previous experience in Private Practice was at Vision Psychology, Mount Gravatt for two years as a Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychologist, and has worked in total in Private Practice for 5 years. Her private practice therapy is client-focused and implements interventions that are evidence-based and primarily focused on ’empowering’ her clients to feel independent, in control of their lives, and to feel a strong sense of hope and trust in themselves and a journey where they can build trust in others around them.

Michelle’s interventions focus mainly on Cognitive-Behaviour Therapy (CBT), Solution-Focused Therapy (SFT), Schema Therapy, Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT), Psychodynamic Therapy and Mindfulness. When working with couples and families, she integrates Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) and Gottman Couples Therapy. Overall, Michelle Barratt Psychology provides psychological therapy for:

Michelle utilises a variety of assessment tools in her sessions to establish a baseline for symptoms, so that progress and outcomes may be reviewed regularly. Additionally, Michelle encourages clients to complete therapy satisfaction surveys to assist her in evaluating therapeutic alliance and the client’s perceived symptom alleviation.

1. Michelle’s Honours thesis focused on exploring the development of a new model of memory put forward by Professor Anne Tolan at the Australian Catholic University (ACU). The statistical significance of these results (The Item/Order Trade-Off Explanation for the Lexicality Effect for Working Memory) has been presented at the International Researchers Memory Conference :

list: In the USA at the University of Massachusetts, October 2010.
The United Kingdom at the University of York, June 2011.

michelle-barratt.p: 2. Michelle’s Masters Degree thesis explored the contribution of a variety of variables that underpinned the dynamics of *Emotional Self-Efficacy* and Subjective Wellbeing. The exploration of emotional self-efficacy was mainly driven by Michelle’s interest in one’s ability to manage trauma. The implicit part of her study focused on someone’s perception of their ability to cope when faced with a trauma and their ‘actual ability’ when faced with a trauma.

High levels of self-esteem significantly support subjective well-being and people who have higher levels of emotional self-efficacy, manage or cope with negative events far better than those who do not. In addition, their ability to do so was found to be mainly supported by a person having higher levels of emotional intelligence and completeing the process of ‘Identity Achievement’.
Michelle was the Student Representative for all Australian Catholic University Students at Masters level during the time she studied.
Emotional self-efficacy: one’s perceived ability to manage their emotions (either positive or negative) when faced with a positive or negative event.

timothy-rach.p: I am a psychologist who recently completed my Master of Clinical Psychology at QUT. Through the Master’s program, I completed two years of practice as a psychologist in the university setting and one year of practice in community mental health.

I primarily work from a psychodynamically-oriented framework, which aims to provide a reflective and secure environment in which my clients are able to develop their understanding of self and relationships with others, based on their experiences, interpretations of these experiences, and emotions. I work with my clients on a regular basis and aim to support them in building an empowered sense of self.

I am interested in working with clients experiencing relationship difficulties, difficulties with personal identity and self-esteem, loss of life satisfaction, difficulties connecting to emotion, recurring patterns in one’s personal and professional life, and life changes or transitions. I am also interested in working with LGBTQIA+ identifying clients.

I have experience working with anxiety, depression, trauma, obsessive-compulsive disorder, ADHD, and Autism. I also have experience in Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT).
I have completed the following qualifications:

list: Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours (University of Queensland)
Master of Clinical Psychology (Queensland University of Technology)

rachel-cleary.p: Rachel Cleary is a General Psychologist
Qualifications: Registered Psychologist (AHPRA Endorsed), B. Psych. Sc. (BA), Psych. Sc. (Hons)
Currently completing PhD in the area of Transcultural Psychology.

Rachel Cleary is a registered psychologist with 15 years of experience. Rachel has worked for over ten years as a psychologist in university settings, and in private practice for 4 years. Rachel has an integrative therapeutic approach, having been trained in a number of diverse therapeutic modalities (Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Schema Therapy, Dialectical Behaviour Therapy, Interpersonal Therapy, Narrative Therapy, Mindfulness and Relaxation, Solution-focussed, Sandplay and ExpressiveTherapies).

Rachel finds each modality offers different strengths and points of focus for therapeutic work. Rachel is happy to see clients with all presentations. Working collaboratively with a client, therapy can be tailored to address the client’s specific personality, issues and context.
Rachel offers counselling to young adolescents, adolescents, young adults, adults and couples. She will work with children as young as 11 years old.
Some of the issues Rachel is able to provide support and guidance for include:

list: Trauma and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)

Stress around life transitions (including adolescence, career change, change in marital or relationship status, pregnancy and motherhood, parenting, migration, cultural adjustment, retirement and end of life issues)
Coping with work pressures (workplace stress, bullying, burn out).
Relationship issues, including separation and divorce.

rachel-cleary.p: Rachel is an ardent lifelong learner and has a commitment to continuing professional development in diverse therapeutic modalities and in treating diverse life issues.

Rachel is also currently completing a PhD at QUT in the area of Transcultural Psychology. Within Australia’s multicultural context, we live in a time of exciting and challenging integration of peoples, cultures and knowledges. This has an impact on the provision of mental health services, and Rachel is passionate about the provision of culturally responsive therapy and mental healthcare for culturally and linguistically diverse clients.

Rachel’s professional practice as a psychologist has been enhanced by previous studies in the humanities, in the areas of culture, language, history and literature. Rachel additionally considers her continuing work with culturally and linguistically diverse peoples and communities (from indigenous, refugee and migrant communities) to be a primary source of her education.

Rachel believes there is much to learn about the art and science of human happiness and mental and emotional wellbeing from diverse cultural and spiritual/wisdom traditions. She is excited by recent, neuroscientific, evidence-based validation for such ancient practices of mental health and wellbeing as mindfulness, meditation and yoga, for the “medicine” or healing potential of storytelling and narrative and for therapeutic work with sand, play and symbol as in Expressive Therapies.

The original Greek meaning of the psyche in psychology is “soul” or “spirit,” and Rachel has found the spiritual dimension to be of central importance for many clients as they navigate life transitions and challenges.

eddie-mtakwa.p: I am a registered psychologist who works with adolescents, adults and couples from a wide range of backgrounds and life experiences. I particularly enjoy working with people experiencing persistent pain, anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship difficulties, work-related stress and major changes in life.

I believe good therapy starts with the relationship between the psychologist and the person sitting in front of them. You do not need to know the right psychological words, have everything figured out, or even know exactly what you want from therapy. Sometimes you simply know that things are not going particularly well and something needs to change. We can start there.

My style as a psychologist is warm, practical and straightforward. I enjoy having a laugh with clients when it is appropriate, but I am equally comfortable sitting with the difficult stuff. I want people to feel that they can talk openly with me without being judged or feeling they need to present a certain version of themselves.
Much of my work involves helping people understand how their mental health is affecting everyday life and then finding practical ways forward.

Persistent pain is an area I particularly enjoy working in. Living with pain can affect far more than the body. It can change how someone sleeps, works, relates to others, sees themselves and thinks about their future. I enjoy helping people understand that relationship and find ways of getting more of their life back, even when the pain itself cannot simply be taken away.

I also enjoy relationship work and helping people who are struggling with work pressures, stress and burnout. Relationships can become difficult when communication breaks down or when work, parenting, financial pressures and other stresses begin following us home. My role is not to decide who is right or wrong. It is to help people understand what is happening, recognise patterns that may be keeping them stuck, and develop healthier ways of responding.

Working with adolescents and young people is another important part of my practice. Young people are navigating relationships, family expectations, education, identity and an increasingly complicated world. I try to give them a space where they can speak honestly and feel heard while also developing practical skills they can use outside therapy.

My therapeutic work draws mainly from Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT)-informed approaches and trauma-focused therapy. I do not believe one approach suits everyone. Therapy should fit the person in front of me and, importantly, it should be useful outside the therapy room.

Before moving into private practice, I spent nine years working within New Zealand’s Department of Corrections Psychological Services. This involved working with people with complex psychological, behavioural and life histories. That experience taught me a great deal about human behaviour, accountability, change and the importance of understanding the person behind the presentation.

My private practice work has included psychological therapy, assessment, rehabilitation and psychological report writing. I have worked with people experiencing trauma, anxiety, depression, persistent pain, adjustment difficulties, workplace issues, relationship difficulties and other complex life circumstances. I am comfortable working alongside other health professionals and value collaborative care where it benefits the person I am working with.

I was born in Zimbabwe and spent much of my professional life in New Zealand before moving to Australia. Having lived and worked across different countries and cultures has shaped the way I practise psychology. Culture, family, identity and life experience matter, and I believe these need to be understood rather than assumed.

Outside of psychology, I’m a husband and dad to three teenagers. Family is a huge part of who I am and, like most people, I know that finding the right balance between everything life throws at you isn’t always easy.
I’m a massive sports fan and love my footy and basketball. I also enjoy CrossFit and getting outdoors, especially camping and four-wheel driving with family and friends.

list: Adjustment to injury, illness and major life changes

eddie-mtakwa.p: Starting therapy can feel like a big step, particularly if you are someone who is used to handling things yourself. You do not need to arrive with everything worked out. We can start with what is happening now, understand what has brought you to this point and work from there.
My aim is for therapy to feel genuine, useful and relevant to your life, not like something that only makes sense for the hour we are sitting together.
I look forward to meeting you.

kimberly-king.p: Hi, I’m Kim. I am a Christian Counsellor dedicated to supporting women and young people (aged 12+) through life’s ups and downs.

So often, we can appear to be coping perfectly well on the outside, while on the inside feeling anxious, stressed, emotionally flat, or completely overwhelmed by the demands of life. I provide a safe, confidential, and non-judgmental space to talk things through.

If you aren’t looking for intensive clinical therapy, but want someone who listens deeply, understands faith and life pressures, and offers practical tools to help you feel more grounded, I am here for you.
I walk alongside you to explore what’s happening beneath the surface, helping you navigate:

list: Life Pressures: Anxiety, stress, burnout, and feeling overwhelmed.
Transitions & Hard Seasons: Grief, loss, parenting challenges, or major life changes.
Identity & Relationships: Relationship strain, intrusive thoughts, or young people trying to figure out who they are and where they’re heading.

kimberly-king.p: Our work together is confidential, collaborative, respectful, and entirely led by you. Because everyone’s comfort zone looks different, you can choose the environment that suits you best:

list: Telehealth (From the comfort of your own space)
Office-Based (A quiet, dedicated counselling room in Toowong)

kimberly-king.p: If you are ready to develop healthy, practical strategies for everyday growth, I invite you to reach out. Let’s take the next step together.

pamela-bray-formas.p: Qualifications: B Psych (QUT); P Grad Dip Psych (Bond)

Pamela is a senior psychologist with 20 years of experience supporting clients across the lifespan. Pamela has a warm, welcoming and empathetic approach and uses a strength based person-centred framework to psychological treatment.

Whilst her practice is evidence-based, Pamela believes in the importance of tailoring treatment to each person to ensure positive long-term outcomes. Using a collaborative approach, Pamela works with other treating professionals and agencies, providing strategies that are both practical and result in excellent outcomes for her clients.

“I support clients of all ages and abilities experiencing anxiety, depression, emotional difficulties, developmental and complex trauma, life transitions, and behavioural challenges. My approach integrates evidence-based modalities, including:

list: Somatic techniques to support regulation, resilience, and psychological well-being”

jennifer-cook.p: Jennifer Cook is a Senior Psychologist
Qualifications: BPsych(Hons) and Registered with AHPRA; Treating: Adults and Children over 15yrs of age

Jenny is a mother of one son and two step-children who understands the demands of juggling work and family life as well as the often complex dynamics of living in a blended family. She enjoys hiking, camping, stand- up paddleboarding and spending time with her two miniature Dachshunds.

She is a registered Psychologist who has been supporting the mental health of clients aged 12+ for over 16 years. Her background is in private practice, Adult Mental Health, private psychiatric hospitals, and school- based settings. She feels privileged to be in a position of trust that enables her to help people to change their relationship with difficult feelings and difficult thoughts and to develop awareness of longstanding, problematic behaviour patterns that can be changed in order to achieve and maintain recovery. She is an empathetic and down-to-earth professional who is passionate about helping people from all walks of life to live a meaningful life.

Using an integrative therapeutic approach she truly enjoys supporting people to overcome a range of problems including adjustment difficulties, mood and behavioural dysregulation, impulsivity, depression, anxiety, anger management, drug & alcohol dependence, loss and grief, interpersonal/relationship issues, Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD), low self-esteem, ADHD assessment and symptoms of trauma.
Seeking help can be tough but making the first step and reaching out will be the start of your recovery journey and she will be there to support you every step of the way.

grant-harvey.p: Grant Harvey brings over fifteen years of experience providing a holistic approach to mental health and wellbeing for individuals, families, and groups. Utilising evidence-based frameworks, Grant works in collaborative partnership with clients to achieve their unique, identified goals.

Prior to his current practice, Grant spent seven years working within the education system, supporting students, families, teachers, and administrative staff. He also extensive experience collaborating with professionals across various industries, assisting them with workplace issues, decision-making processes, and communication strategies.
An experienced facilitator, Grant has written and delivered several highly successful group-work programs for young people in schools across Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland.

Known for his relaxed and welcoming style, Grant creates an environment where clients feel comfortable from their very first session. He breaks down complex psychological concepts into simple, actionable strategies that clients can easily understand and apply to their daily lives.
